label: D2 after choosing a1 and landing in S2 (a1 rare transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when this trial's choice was a1 (last-action input = a1). Strong activations (about 0.7-1.0 of max) come almost entirely from a1 followed by the rare transition to S2. The predicate D2 & action==1 & state==2 has dev precision 0.985 and mass recall 0.96 (correlation 0.98). F1 is only 0.76 because of a large tail of very weak activations (about 0.02-0.15 of max) at D2 after a1 -> S1 common. Those steps account for about 40% of active steps but only 4% of activation mass. It never fires at D1 or GO, and essentially never after a2 (227 steps), whichever state follows. Beyond that, I did not check what drives the size of the activation. All variables are observed at D2, so no future variables are used.

issues: Each claim checks out on dev. The feature has zero activations at D1 or GO and 100% of its activation mass at D2. After a2, D2 has only 227 active steps (precision 0.001, mass 0.0001). On test the predicate scores precision 0.983, recall 0.595, F1 0.741 and mass recall 0.954, matching the report.

The weak tail at D2 after a1 -> S1 common is real. That predicate has precision 0.22, recall 0.38 and mass recall 0.041, and those steps fill the bottom activation quartile. I found no clean subset to explain it. Splitting by good state gives good=S1 at precision 0.21 and mass 0.031, and good=S2 at precision 0.42 but recall 0.04. Splitting by prev_action or prev_reward leaves precision at 0.19-0.24 throughout. So it looks like diffuse low-level leakage rather than a missed class.

On the test split, the false positives (787 steps, about 1.7% of predicted) and the missed activations (4.6% of activation mass) look scattered. They show no systematic phase, trial position, reward or good-state pattern. Minor caveat: the label leaves out the weak a1 -> S1 tail, which the explanation does acknowledge.
